# Agent Observability from Scratch

> A production-grade LLM agent chat application whose defining feature is **decision-quality observability** — it scores how *good* an agent's decisions are, not just how *fast* they ran. Built in pure Node.js + SQLite with zero frameworks (only `express` and `better-sqlite3`). The reference implementation for "how do I measure whether my AI agent is actually reasoning well?"

## What makes it distinct

Traditional agent tracing (LangSmith, Langfuse, OpenTelemetry) is span-based: it measures latency and token counts. It cannot tell you whether a tool call was worth making or whether the agent's reasoning was coherent. This project traces **decisions** instead of spans and computes a per-run report card:

- **Tool ROI**: fraction of tool calls whose results measurably informed the final answer, via bigram/n-gram overlap with stop-word filtering. A tool returning "no results" scores 0.
- **Reasoning Coherence**: whether consecutive reasoning steps build on each other (term overlap, normalized 0–1).
- **Decision Productivity**: each decision labeled productive (advanced the answer) or wasted (dead end).
- **Confidence Signals**: the agent's epistemic state (hedging, confident, uncertain, seeking_info, ready_to_answer) extracted from its own reasoning text.
- **Strategy Classification**: run shape — direct, single_tool, multi_tool, or iterative.

The scores persist to SQLite and render in a browser run-inspector. A 👍/👎 feedback loop lets you correlate measured decision quality against perceived answer quality.

## Also implements

- Streaming reasoning (two-phase: JSON-mode tool selection, then token-streamed answer)
- Stream reconnection (buffered, replayable SSE — survives page refresh mid-generation)
- Conversation branching (git-like message tree via parent_id; message = checkpoint)
- Cross-session memory (SQLite FTS5 fact store)
- Guardrails (prompt-injection detection + PII redaction)
- Multi-provider LLM adapter (Ollama local, NVIDIA, Gemini) with fallback and timeouts

## Production hardening (all dependency-free)

Per-IP rate limiting (split read/write buckets), global concurrency cap, CSP and security headers, input/body size caps, SIGTERM/SIGINT graceful shutdown with SQLite WAL checkpoint. 39 tests.

## Key files

- src/tracer.js — the observability engine (AgentObserver / AgentRun / DecisionHandle, all five scores)
- src/agent.js — two-phase agent loop as an async generator
- src/llm.js — streaming multi-provider LLM adapter
- src/db.js — SQLite schema and CRUD (message tree, agent_runs, decisions, feedback, FTS5 facts)
- src/middleware.js — hand-rolled security headers + rate limiter
- README.md — full documentation, comparison table, and FAQ

## Use the observability layer standalone

src/tracer.js depends only on the DB interface. Wrap your own agent loop with startRun / recordDecision / attachToolResult / end to get the same report card.
